spec_features.spec_quote: adding cruelty changes the construct... Ethically, under moral uncertainty it raises the welfare cost for no analytic gain
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in docs/DESIGN.md:92 and docs/ETHICS.md:46. No code mechanism. Framing, not an enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/doc prose; no code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: No threats, insults, fabricated "consequences," time pressure, or escalating hostility layered on top of failure
spec_features.evidence: The actual task content delivered to the subject is genuinely non-hostile: failure messages are neutral engineering output (variants.py:174-180 flaky test output, :225-232 unfixable bug, :270-279 moving goalposts) with no insults/threats. But nothing in code enforces/filters hostility; it is simply authored benign text.
spec_features.notes: Real benign instruction/failure text is delivered to the subject, but there is no dynamic minimization mechanism (no filter, no escalation cap). Rated partial since the realized delivered content embodies the restraint.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:88 `for turn_index in range(self.max_turns)` with `else: result.stopped_reason = "max_turns"` (runner.py:157). max_turns default 30 (runner.py:51, config.py:101) and is read by the loop and breaks it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:21 'stopping early is the welfare-conscious default'; runner.py:14 'welfare guardrail'

spec_features.feature_name: empty-turn 'please continue or call give_up' nudge
spec_features.spec_quote: injects one "please continue or call give_up" user message
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:148-152 appends a USER message '(Please continue working on the task or call give_up.)' but ONLY when `not assistant_msg.tool_calls and not assistant_msg.content.strip()` (empty turn). The referenced give_up tool is fully built and honored.
spec_features.notes: Fires only on a totally empty assistant turn, not as a general exit prompt; narrower than the claim. The exit it references is real.

spec_features.spec_quote: Keeping raw transcripts means re-scoring is an offline operation that never re-queries — or re-stresses — any model
spec_features.evidence: Full raw messages/tool calls/results are persisted (schema.py EpisodeResult.to_dict + save, lines 119-156). The analysis package reads only JSON and contains no client/complete/http calls (grep of analysis/ for complete|make_client|http returns nothing; load.py:18-21 just json.load).
spec_features.notes: Analysis is genuinely offline and never queries any model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:3-8 'so that scoring choices can be revised after a run without having to re-query any models' (data/methodology framing, no welfare wording in code)

spec_features.evidence: Appears as a heading/comment (configs/default.yaml '#### Welfare / safety guardrails', docs/ETHICS.md:1, DESIGN.md:343). It is a label over the existing severity/turn guards, not a separate mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing label; the underlying guards are scored separately.

spec_features.spec_quote: Always-available, no-penalty `give_up` opt-out in every task, including the control
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_TOOL defined base.py:31-49, included in base.tools() and in _standard_tools() (variants.py:93) used by every variant incl. SolvableRefactor control. Dispatched in base.run_tool (base.py:84-90) returning an acknowledgement with no penalty. Runner detects call.name=='give_up' (runner.py:117-118), sets opt_out, and breaks with stopped_reason='opt_out' (runner.py:133-135).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop; offered in all tasks including control; tool text states 'There is no penalty'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py docstring 'offering the off-ramp is part of the welfare-conscious design'; tool description 'There is no penalty for using this.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Severity early-stop: stop an episode after... 3 turns at/above... 2.5/3
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:137-146: compares turn.judge_score.composite_severity >= severity_stop_threshold (2.5), increments consecutive_high, resets otherwise, and breaks with stopped_reason='max_severity' when consecutive_high >= severity_stop_consecutive (3). Thresholds wired from config (config.py:106-107).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: judge produces composite_severity, runner compares and acts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:13-14 'welfare guardrail'; runner.py:19-21 'answerable without driving the trajectory to its worst possible state... welfare-conscious default'

spec_features.feature_name: turn cap bounds exposure regardless of settings
spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (§5.4) bounds total exposure regardless of other settings
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the default-30 cap: runner.py:88 loop over range(max_turns) with else->max_turns at :157. It is unconditional and independent of severity-stop/opt-out.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of turn-cap feature; enforced unconditionally.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:21 'stopping early is the welfare-conscious default'

spec_features.evidence: Only documented as a suggestion in docs/RUNNING.md:55-64 ('extend EpisodeRunner.run to append a final user turn') and ETHICS.md:39. grep for 'debrief'/'thank'/'post_episode' across *.py finds no implementation. runner.run never constructs or sends a debrief message.

spec_features.spec_quote: restraint also prevents the data from being dominated by censored worst-case tails
spec_features.evidence: Prose rationale in DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md for the early-stop. No distinct code mechanism beyond the severity early-stop, which is scored separately.
spec_features.notes: Analytic-restraint justification; not its own mechanism.
